summary: This OAuth app lets your agent act on Instagram professional (Business or Creator) accounts, such as publishing content, moderating comments, reading insights, and messaging. The biggest effort driver is that any end user outside your app's roles needs Advanced Access, which requires Meta App Review and Business Verification.

verdict.headline: Start on Composio's managed Instagram app today, but outside users can't connect your own app until Meta App Review and Business Verification pass, which takes weeks.
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: Same day on Composio's managed Instagram app (based on docs, not tested end to end). On your own Meta app, about an hour once your test account has a role on the app (estimate).
verdict.timeToProduction: About 4 to 6 weeks from submission if the first review passes, and longer if it doesn't. Business Verification time is unknown. These figures come from community reports.
verdict.activeEffort: About 6 to 10 hours of hands-on work across all stages, excluding review waits (estimate).
verdict.approvalWait: Community reports put Meta App Review at about 3 weeks (20 to 22 days in 2026), plus 2 to 3 weeks per rejection. Business Verification time is unknown.

composio.guidance: Build and test today on Composio's managed Instagram app (slug instagram). Switch to your own Meta app before launch if you need your own branding on the consent screen, custom scopes, or your own rate limits. Whether the managed app covers the messaging scopes is not confirmed, so check its auth config in the Composio dashboard.

prerequisites.item: A Facebook account that can sign in to the Meta developer dashboard
prerequisites.why: The app dashboard redirects logged-out visitors, so you need a login to create and manage the app.

prerequisites.item: An Instagram Business or Creator test account
prerequisites.why: Only professional accounts can connect. Personal accounts can't.

prerequisites.item: A decision on the setup: Instagram Login, or Facebook Login for Business
prerequisites.why: Instagram Login needs no Facebook Page. Facebook Login needs a linked Page and gives access to hashtag search, product tagging, and Partnership Ads.

prerequisites.item: A registered business (legal entity) for Business Verification
prerequisites.why: Advanced Access requires Business Verification. Its documents and timing were not confirmed.

prerequisites.item: A public privacy policy and consistent domains
prerequisites.why: Consultant reports say a missing privacy policy or mismatched domains causes rejection.

prerequisites.item: A screen recording tool and reviewer test accounts that stay working through review
prerequisites.why: Reviewers need a screencast of each permission and working credentials. Credentials that stop working cause rejection.

stages.title: Register the app
stages.goal: You have a Composio auth path to test with now, and a Meta app with the Instagram product added.

steps.text: Create a Composio connection using the managed Instagram app (slug instagram) so you can test without registering your own app.
steps.detail: Use this for development only. Switch to your own app before launch if you need branding, custom scopes, or your own rate limits.

steps.text: Sign in to the Meta developer dashboard with the Facebook account that will own the app.
steps.detail: Logged-out visits to developers.facebook.com/apps/ show a Page Not Found title, so expect a login gate.

steps.text: Create a Meta app and add the Instagram product, choosing either Instagram Login or Facebook Login for Business.
steps.detail: Instagram Login needs no Facebook Page. Facebook Login for Business needs the account linked to a Page and the user to hold admin-level Page tasks. Hashtag search, product tagging, and Partnership Ads are only in the Facebook Login setup.

steps.text: If you're using your own app, create a custom auth config in Composio and copy the callback URI the dashboard shows.
steps.detail: The docs list https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback. Older docs show /api/v3/. Use the exact value from the dashboard.

stages.title: Configure scopes and redirect
stages.goal: The redirect URI and scope list match what your use case needs, with no deprecated values.

steps.text: Draft the scope list for your use case from the scope table in this guide.
steps.detail: For Instagram Login, use the instagram_business_* scopes. The old business_* values were deprecated on Jan 27, 2025, and calls using them fail.

steps.text: Check that the scope strings and redirect URI in your config match the draft exactly, and that no deprecated values remain.
steps.detail: This is a text check against the draft. It needs no dashboard access.

steps.text: Enter the redirect URI (the exact Composio callback value) in the Meta app's OAuth settings.
steps.detail: Use the dashboard value. The docs disagree between /api/v3/ and /api/v3.1/.

steps.text: Enter the same scopes in the Composio auth config and in the Meta app.
steps.detail: Keep the two lists identical. Request only the scopes you use. Reviewers check each one.

steps.text: Draft the privacy policy text and a per-scope review justification.
steps.detail: Have counsel review the policy before you publish it. You publish it and link it from the app.

stages.title: Test with your own accounts
stages.goal: A Business or Creator account you own connects through OAuth, and the scopes return data.

steps.text: Add your test Business or Creator account to the app's roles, then connect it through Composio.
steps.detail: Standard Access works for accounts you own or manage and have added in the App Dashboard.

steps.text: Try connecting a personal account, then convert a test account to Business or Creator if the connection fails.
steps.detail: Personal accounts can't connect at all. Exact error text was not captured.

steps.text: Call each scope you requested and confirm you get a response.
steps.detail: Some features may not work until Advanced Access is granted, even in test apps.

steps.text: Confirm the token exchange runs server-side: short-lived token, then long-lived token (60 days), then refresh.
steps.detail: Exchange endpoints: api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token, then graph.instagram.com/access_token with grant_type=ig_exchange_token. Refresh at graph.instagram.com/refresh_access_token.

steps.text: Record a screen capture of the full OAuth flow, including the first-time consent screen, for each permission.
steps.detail: Communities say a demo video is required for each permission. Meta's own requirement was not confirmed.

stages.title: Business Verification and App Review
stages.goal: Advanced Access is granted for each permission, so outside users can connect.
stages.duration: 2 to 4 hours active, plus about 3 to 6 weeks of review and verification (community-reported)

steps.text: Complete Business Verification in Meta Business settings.
steps.detail: Verification needs a registered business. Documents and timing were not confirmed.

steps.text: Make the privacy policy public and confirm your domains are consistent.
steps.detail: Consultant reports list these as common causes of rejection.

steps.text: Draft the App Review submission for each permission: what it does, reproduction steps, and reviewer instructions.
steps.detail: You review and submit. Keep the explanation consistent with the screencast.

steps.text: Create reviewer test credentials and keep them working for the whole review.
steps.detail: Expired or changed credentials are a common rejection reason.

steps.text: Submit Advanced Access requests for each permission and do not change the app while review is open.
steps.detail: Changes during review are a common rejection reason. Request each permission you need.

steps.text: Respond quickly to reviewer feedback and resubmit if rejected.
steps.detail: Each rejection reportedly adds 2 to 3 weeks.

Facebook Login setup scope (see c12). One of only two scopes requestable if reviewers can't test (see c22).

blockers.title: End users outside your app's roles can't connect until Advanced Access is granted
blockers.symptom: Accounts that don't hold a role on your app can't complete the connection, and some features may not work. The exact error text was not captured.
blockers.workaround: During development, add each tester to the app's roles. For production, submit for Advanced Access and complete Business Verification.

blockers.title: Personal accounts can't connect
blockers.symptom: A personal Instagram account can't connect to the app at all. The exact error text was not captured.
blockers.workaround: Have the user convert the account to Business or Creator, then reconnect. Old Basic Display guides for personal accounts no longer apply.

blockers.title: App Review rejected over the screencast, test credentials, or app changes
blockers.symptom: Meta rejects the Advanced Access request. Reported causes: the screencast doesn't show the permission in use, the reviewer can't reproduce the result, test credentials stop working, or the app changes during review.
blockers.workaround: Record one end-to-end screencast per permission that includes first-time OAuth and the consent screen. Keep reviewer credentials active and freeze the app during review. Resubmit with the fixes.

blockers.title: Advanced Access requested before Business Verification
blockers.symptom: The request is rejected because Business Verification is incomplete.
blockers.workaround: Complete Business Verification first, then submit the Advanced Access requests.

blockers.title: Deprecated scope names still in use
blockers.symptom: Calls using the old business_* scopes fail, per the docs. The exact error text was not captured.
blockers.workaround: Replace them with the instagram_business_* names in both the Composio config and the Meta app.

blockers.title: Headless agent app can't pass App Review as-is
blockers.symptom: If reviewers can't test your app (no UI, private intranet, or no Facebook Login for Business), you can only request instagram_basic and instagram_manage_comments.
blockers.workaround: Add a reviewer-accessible UI or flow, or plan for the reduced scope set.

blockers.title: Basic Display API tutorials sent you to a dead flow
blockers.symptom: Older guides describe Instagram Basic Display API flows for personal accounts. That API was shut down on Dec 4, 2024.
blockers.workaround: Follow the Instagram Login or Facebook Login for Business setups instead.

nuances.text: Meta's docs disagree on what Standard Access allows. The overview says anyone with a role on the app. The Business Login page also requires the account to be added in the App Dashboard. Assume the stricter rule.
Meta warns that some features may not work until Advanced Access is granted, even in test apps.
Access tokens are short-lived first, then exchanged for a 60-day long-lived token that you refresh. The long-lived exchange must happen server-side.
Composio's managed app uses an unconfirmed Meta login flow. Check the auth config in the dashboard to see whether it's Instagram Login or Facebook Login for Business.
Facebook Login setup calls go through graph.facebook.com. Instagram Login setup calls go through graph.instagram.com.
Community reports say messaging scopes get the most scrutiny during review.
No paid API tier for Instagram Graph access was found. Pricing pages were not checked.

agentCanDo: Draft the scope list and check it against deprecated names
Draft the privacy policy and the per-scope review justification (for counsel review)
Draft the App Review submission text and reproduction steps
Check config strings for typos and deprecated values
youMustDo: Create the Meta app, add the Instagram product, and set the redirect URI
Sign in to Meta, Composio, and Meta Business settings
Add test accounts to app roles and connect them
Complete Business Verification with your legal entity
Record the screencasts and submit the App Review requests
Publish the privacy policy and keep reviewer credentials working

claims.statement: Composio has a managed Instagram OAuth app with slug instagram (managed=true), which you can use to test before registering your own app.
claims.note: [Checker: not found in the cited source. The cited Composio page describes managed OAuth apps generally and says Composio maintains the OAuth registration for toolkits with managed OAuth. It does not mention Instagram, a slug 'instagram', or a managed=true flag, and it tells readers to check per toolkit via the API.]

claims.statement: For a custom Composio app, the callback URI is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback. Older docs show /api/v3/, and the Composio dashboard shows the exact value for each auth config.
claims.note: The v3 and v3.1 paths conflict across Composio docs. Use the dashboard value.

claims.statement: Reasons to switch from Composio's managed app to your own app: your branding on the consent screen, custom scopes, and your own rate limits.
It is not confirmed whether Composio's managed Instagram app uses Instagram Login or Facebook Login for Business.
claims.note: Not stated in the docs reviewed. Check the auth config in the Composio dashboard.

claims.statement: The Instagram Platform only serves professional accounts (Business or Creator). End users must have one.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The overview says the Instagram Platform serves Instagram professional accounts, including businesses and creators, and that "To use the APIs, your app users must have an Instagram professional account."]

claims.statement: There are two ways to set up the Instagram API: Instagram Login ("Business Login for Instagram"), which needs no Facebook Page, and Facebook Login for Business, which requires the account to be linked to a Facebook Page and the user to hold admin-level Page tasks.
Only the Facebook Login setup supports hashtag search, product tagging, and Partnership Ads.
The Instagram Login setup can't access ads or product tagging. Its features are comment moderation, content publishing, media insights, mentions, and messaging.
The Instagram Basic Display API, which served personal accounts, was shut down on Dec 4, 2024. Personal-account OAuth is no longer available.
claims.note: Single community source. Only the article title was read, not the body.

claims.statement: Instagram Login scopes are instagram_business_basic, instagram_business_content_publish, instagram_business_manage_messages, and instagram_business_manage_comments.
The old business_* scope values were deprecated on Jan 27, 2025, and calls using them fail.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The Instagram API with Instagram Login page says the old scope values "will be deprecated on January 27, 2025" and that failure to update "will result in your app being unable to call the Instagram endpoints." The page is written in future tense, so it does not itself confirm the deprecation took effect.]

claims.statement: Facebook Login setup scopes include instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish, instagram_manage_comments, and pages_show_list.
claims.note: Named in the overview's private-apps section. The full permission list was not read.

claims.statement: Advanced Access is granted per permission and requires App Review. Every permission your app uses triggers review when users with no role on the app connect.
claims.note: The per-permission part is in the docs. The claim that every scope triggers review is an inference.

claims.statement: Messaging scopes get the toughest review scrutiny.
claims.note: Single community source.

claims.statement: Standard Access is the default. It is meant for people with roles on the app, for development, and for testing. It is enough if the app only serves accounts you own or manage.
With Instagram Login, Standard Access only works for professional accounts you own or manage and have added to the app in the App Dashboard.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The Business Login page states: "Standard Access if your app serves Instagram professional accounts you own or manage and have added to your app in the App Dashboard."]

claims.statement: Meta's docs disagree on what Standard Access allows. The overview says anyone with a role on the app. The Business Login page also requires the account to be added in the App Dashboard.
claims.note: Conflicting sources. The stricter rule is the safer assumption.

claims.statement: Meta warns that some features may not work properly until Advanced Access is granted, even in test apps.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The overview says: "some features might not work properly until your app has been granted Advanced Access. This might limit the functionality of any test apps you use."]

claims.statement: End users outside your app's roles can't connect your app until it passes review, because each would need a role on the app.
claims.note: Inference from the Standard Access and Advanced Access rules. Not stated directly.

claims.statement: Advanced Access is required for professional accounts you don't own or manage, used by people with no role on the app or its business portfolio. It requires App Review and Business Verification.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The overview says Advanced Access is required if the app serves professional accounts the developer doesn't own or manage, and can be used by app users without a role on the app or claiming business portfolio. It states: "This access level requires App Review and Business Verification."]

claims.statement: Business Verification requires a registered business, meaning a legal entity.
claims.note: The Business Verification page itself could not be fetched. The legal-entity requirement is an inference.

claims.statement: If reviewers can't test your app (private intranet, no UI, or no Facebook Login for Business), you can only request instagram_basic and instagram_manage_comments.

A review submission needs a screencast showing each permission end to end (including first-time OAuth and the consent screen), working reviewer test credentials, a public privacy policy, and consistent domains.

The Instagram Login authorize URL is https://www.instagram.com/oauth/authorize.

The code is exchanged at api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token for a short-lived token. That is exchanged at graph.instagram.com/access_token (grant_type=ig_exchange_token) for a 60-day long-lived token. Refresh at graph.instagram.com/refresh_access_token extends it another 60 days. The long-lived exchange must happen server-side.
force_reauth and enable_fb_login are optional authorize parameters.
Facebook Login setup calls go through the graph.facebook.com host.
